nodes.text:
Nifty dropped by 400 points…while the India VIX surged by 14%... Concerns over HMPV being the latest threat, along with weak Asian markets and anticipation of TCS's Q3 results this week, contributed to the market decline.

The equity benchmark Nifty dropped nearly 400 points,

nodes.author: MOResearch360
nodes.text: PSU banks, real estate, and oil and gas stocks were among the hardest hit. Bank of Baroda, PNB, and Canara Bank each saw a drop of around 4%, while major stocks like HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries (RIL), and Kotak Mahindra Bank were significant contributors to the Sensex decline.

nodes.author: MOResearch360
nodes.text: The India VIX, a gauge of market fear, surged 14% as a broad sell-off affected mid and small-cap stocks across various sectors. The Sensex hit a day's low of 78,300, falling over 950 points, while the Nifty slid close to 300 points, nearing the 23,700 mark.

nodes.author: MOResearch360
nodes.text:
and the Sensex plunged over 900 points, driven by weak Asian markets and concerns ahead of IT giant TCS's quarterly results this week.

Additionally, reports of the first HMPV case detected in Bengaluru, coupled with a virus outbreak in China, weighed on market sentiment.
